bull_case: Vertiv redeploys rapidly rising cash flow into capacity, engineering, liquid cooling and power adjacencies at high incremental returns while per-share FCF compounds with minimal dilution.
bear_case: Current returns are inflated by backlog scarcity and working-capital inflows; capacity and acquisition spending earn lower returns once hyperscaler capex normalizes.
thesis: Reinvestment quality is strong. From 2023 to 2025, operating profit and FCF/share expanded sharply with modest dilution, while engineering R&D and capex remained meaningful but absorbable. H1 2026 cash flow is unusually strong and includes a large working-capital source, so the score does not extrapolate that run-rate. Using FY2025 as the disclosed fallback, capex plus R&D absorbed about 31% of OCF, consistent with a healthy but not maximal internal reinvestment rate.

evidence.claim: Raw FCF/share rose from about $2.00 in 2023 to $2.98 in 2024 and $4.85 in 2025 using OCF minus capex divided by diluted shares.
Operating profit rose from $872.2M in 2023 to $1.367B in 2024 and $1.830B in 2025 while diluted shares remained near 386-391M.

FY2025 capex plus engineering R&D was $661.7M versus $2.114B of OCF, an internal absorption rate of about 31%; TTM R&D is not separately available, so the rubric fallback uses the latest full fiscal year.
H1 2026 OCF was $1.867B but included a $678.8M working-capital source, requiring normalization before extrapolating FCF.

counterevidence: Current FCF benefits from deferred-revenue and other working-capital inflows.
Capacity capex is rising and may earn lower returns after backlog normalizes.
UIG and PurgeRite increase M&A capital intensity and integration risk.
Historical returns were achieved from a much smaller revenue base.
unknowns: True TTM R&D and maintenance capex split.
Post-close UIG return on invested capital.
Normalized working-capital needs after backlog stabilizes.
falsifiers: If FCF/share falls for two years despite sales growth, quality score should be reduced.
If new capacity sustains margins and converts backlog without excess inventory, incremental ROIC remains high.
If acquisition goodwill/impairments emerge or pro-forma leverage rises without FCF growth, reinvestment quality deteriorates.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Multi-year operating profit and FCF/share expansion provide direct evidence of improving incremental returns rather than collapse.
Diluted share count increased only modestly from 2023 to 2025 while FCF/share rose materially.

key_kpis.name: FCF/share
key_kpis.threshold: compound at least low/mid-teens over cycle

key_kpis.name: inventory vs sales
key_kpis.threshold: inventory growth normalize with backlog conversion

key_kpis.name: incremental operating profit / capital deployed
key_kpis.threshold: remain well above cost of capital

subscores.rationale: Operating profit and FCF/share rose rapidly from 2023-2025 with modest share growth and manageable capital spending.
FY2025 fallback absorption was about 31%, inside the 15%-35% rubric band and supported by multiple capacity/R&D/adjacency projects.
Raw FCF/share more than doubled from 2023 to 2025 with low dilution; H1 2026 working-capital help is explicitly not treated as normalized.

uncertainties.rationale: The current investment wave has not completed a full cycle.
TTM R&D is unavailable, requiring the rubric's latest-FY fallback.
2026 cash conversion is temporarily boosted by working capital.
